module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-! # The Poincaré Conjecture

References:
- [Miln2022](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/poincare.pdf)
- [Wang2017](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2017/186-2/p03).
- [mo296171](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/296171/unique-smooth-structure-on-3-manifolds)
- [mathlib4](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4)

The formalisations in this file are based on the ones written by Junyan Xu in Mathlib4.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u

namespace PoincareConjecture

open scoped Manifold ContDiff EuclideanGeometry ContinuousMap

local macro:max "𝕊" noWs n:superscript(term) : term =>
  `(Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin ($(⟨n.raw[0]⟩) + 1))) 1)

/-- The predicate that the generalized Poincaré conjecture holds in dimension $n$, i.e. that
any $n$-dimensional manifold that is homotopy equivalent to the sphere is in fact homeomorphic
to the sphere. -/
def ConjectureFor (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace (ℝ^n) M], M ≃ₕ 𝕊ⁿ → Nonempty (M ≃ₜ 𝕊ⁿ)

/--
The Millennium Problem, solved by Grigori Perelman in 2003: the Poincaré Conjecture holds.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture : ConjectureFor 3 := by
  sorry

/--
The Generalized Poincaré Conjecture holds for surfaces.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.dimension_two : ConjectureFor 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The Generalized Poincaré Conjecture holds for dimensions at least 5.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.dimension_ge_five (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) : ConjectureFor n := by
  sorry

/--
The Generalized Poincaré Conjecture holds in dimension 4.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.dimension_four : ConjectureFor 4 := by
  sorry

/-- The predicate that the smooth Poincaré conjecture holds in dimension $n$, i.e. that any
smooth $n$-dimensional manifold that is homotopy equivalent to the sphere is in fact diffeomorphic
to the sphere. As in `ConjectureFor`, the manifold must be Hausdorff: `ChartedSpace` and
`IsManifold` do not imply this, and in every positive dimension there is a non-Hausdorff smooth
manifold that is homotopy equivalent to the sphere. -/
def SmoothConjectureFor (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type u) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace (ℝ^n) M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M], M ≃ₕ 𝕊ⁿ → Nonempty (M ≃ₘ⟮𝓡 n, 𝓡 n⟯ 𝕊ⁿ)

/-- A reformulation of the Millennium Problem in terms of smooth 3-folds. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_for_three : SmoothConjectureFor 3 := by
  sorry

/-- The smooth formulation of the Millennium Problem implies the general case. This follows from
the fact that every topological 3-fold admits a smooth structure [mo296171]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_implication (H : SmoothConjectureFor 3) :
    ConjectureFor 3 := by
  sorry

/-- The values at which the smooth version of the conjecture is known to hold. -/
def SmoothTrueValues : Set ℕ := {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 12, 56, 61}

/-- The smooth version of the Poincaré conjecture is known to hold in dimensions
$1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 12, 56, 61$. See [Wang2017]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_known_cases (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ SmoothTrueValues) :
    SmoothConjectureFor n := by
  sorry

/-- The four dimensional case of the smooth version of the conjecture is still open.
See [Wang2017]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_dimension_four : SmoothConjectureFor 4 := by
  sorry

/-- It is conjectured that the only values of $n > 4$ for which the smooth version of the
conjecture holds are $n = 5, 6, 12, 56, 61$. See Conjecture 1.17 in [Wang2017]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_other_cases (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 4)
    (hn' : n ∉ SmoothTrueValues) : ¬ SmoothConjectureFor n := by
  sorry

end PoincareConjecture

reformulations.difference: The Clay problem (Milnor) is about closed (compact) 3-manifolds that are simply connected: "every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere". The generalized conjecture (Wang–Xu, Question 1.2) is about closed n-manifolds homotopy equivalent to S^n. `ConjectureFor n` instead quantifies over every `M : Type` with a topology, `T2Space`, and a `ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))` atlas. It assumes no compactness, connectedness, second countability or paracompactness, and its hypothesis is `M ≃ₕ 𝕊ⁿ`. For n = 3 (`poincare_conjecture`) that hypothesis replaces "simply connected closed". The same definition is used by `variants.dimension_two`, `variants.dimension_four` and `variants.dimension_ge_five`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Let M be Hausdorff and locally Euclidean of dimension n ≥ 1 with M ≃ₕ Sⁿ. Then M is path-connected, and H_n(M;ℤ/2) ≅ H_n(Sⁿ;ℤ/2) = ℤ/2 ≠ 0. Hatcher defines an n-manifold as "a Hausdorff space M in which each point has an open neighborhood homeomorphic to Rⁿ", with no second countability. His Prop. 3.29 says: "If M is a connected noncompact n-manifold, then H_i(M;R) = 0 for i ≥ n." So M is compact. Being compact, it is covered by finitely many charts, so it is second countable and metrizable: a closed n-manifold in the usual sense. Conversely, every closed n-manifold is an instance of the Lean hypotheses. So `ConjectureFor n` is exactly the generalized Poincaré conjecture in dimension n. (2) For n = 3, a closed 3-manifold is simply connected iff it is homotopy equivalent to S³ (Poincaré duality, Hurewicz, Whitehead). Wang–Xu state this explicitly: "a closed 3-manifold is simply connected if and only if it is homotopy equivalence to the 3-sphere". So `ConjectureFor 3` is equivalent to the Clay statement. (3) Restricting to `Type` (universe 0) is harmless: compact manifolds embed in some ℝ^N. `T2Space` is required, as in the standard definition of a manifold.

reformulations.difference: Wang–Xu pose the smooth question as "Let M be a closed n-manifold. Suppose M is homeomorphic to Sⁿ. Is M diffeomorphic to Sⁿ?" (Question 1.4). Conjecture 1.17 is phrased as "the only spheres with a unique smooth structure are S⁵, S⁶, S¹², S⁵⁶, S⁶¹" for dimensions greater than 4. The Lean predicate instead says: every Hausdorff C^∞ n-manifold (not assumed compact or second countable) that is homotopy equivalent to Sⁿ is C^∞-diffeomorphic to Mathlib's sphere with its stereographic atlas. `smooth_other_cases` states only the "only" direction, written as n > 4 ∧ n ∉ SmoothTrueValues → ¬SmoothConjectureFor n. This predicate is used by `smooth_known_cases`, `smooth_dimension_four`, `smooth_other_cases`, `smooth_for_three` and `smooth_implication`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Compactness follows from the homology argument above (Hatcher Prop. 3.29), so M is a closed smooth manifold. Homotopy equivalent and homeomorphic are the same for closed n-manifolds in every dimension, by the topological generalized Poincaré conjecture (Wang–Xu Thm 1.3: Smale, Newman, Connell, Freedman, Perelman). Orientation does not matter, because Sⁿ has an orientation-reversing diffeomorphism. Hence SmoothConjectureFor n ⟺ "Sⁿ has a unique smooth structure" (⟺ Θ_n = 0 for n ≥ 5). This also matches Milnor's Clay wording for n = 4: "It is not known whether every smooth homotopy 4-sphere is diffeomorphic to S⁴". I checked in Lean that `∞` elaborates to `↑(⊤ : ℕ∞)` (C^∞, not ω) and that the sphere's charts are Mathlib's stereographic atlas. I also proved in Lean that SmoothTrueValues ∩ {n | 4 < n} = {5, 6, 12, 56, 61}, so `smooth_other_cases` is exactly the "only" of Conjecture 1.17. The "if" direction is the known result `smooth_known_cases`.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1601.02184 (LaTeX source: Conjecture 1.17, Questions 1.2/1.4, Theorem 1.3, Theorem 1.14, Corollary 1.15, Remark 1.16)

review.notes:
No mathematical defect found. Details for maintainers:

(1) Lean checks. Both definitions unfold (by `Iff.rfl`) to the expected statements: the sphere is `Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+1))) 1`, `ℝ^n` is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, and both `IsManifold` and `≃ₘ⟮𝓡 n, 𝓡 n⟯` use `∞ = ↑(⊤ : ℕ∞)`, i.e. C^∞ and not analytic. The sphere's charted-space instance is Mathlib's stereographic atlas, which is the standard smooth structure. Both predicates have satisfiable hypotheses: the standard sphere satisfies them, and the conclusion holds for it via `refl`. So neither predicate is vacuous or trivially false.

(2) Missing compactness and second countability. This is not a gap: a Hausdorff n-manifold homotopy equivalent to Sⁿ (n ≥ 1) is automatically compact (Hatcher Prop. 3.29 with ℤ/2 coefficients), hence second countable. n = 0 never occurs in any theorem.

(3) The `T2Space` hypothesis is necessary, and the `SmoothConjectureFor` docstring is right to say so. Mathlib's original `NonemptyDiffeomorphSphere` omits it. The docstring's claim that a non-Hausdorff counterexample exists in every positive dimension is correct. Example: two copies of ℝⁿ glued along the complement of the closed unit ball. The map (x,i) ↦ (2x,i) is homotopic to the identity via (1+t)x and factors through the Hausdorff quotient, which is homotopy equivalent to Sⁿ. (ℝⁿ with a doubled origin would not work: every map from it to Sⁿ factors through ℝⁿ.)

(4) Categories (not a mathematical issue, and not open/solved staleness). `variants.dimension_four` (Freedman's theorem) and `variants.smooth_for_three` are tagged `textbook`. `smooth_for_three` is equivalent to the Millennium problem via Moise, and its own docstring calls it a reformulation of it. Yet `poincare_conjecture` is tagged `research solved`, so `research solved` would be more consistent for both.

(5) Status. All categories match the sources:
- `smooth_dimension_four` is still open (Wikipedia: whether exotic 4-spheres exist is unsolved).
- `smooth_other_cases` (Wang–Xu Conjecture 1.17) is still open. Odd dimensions are settled by Wang–Xu, and even dimensions below 140 by Behrens–Hill–Hopkins–Mahowald, both consistent with the conjecture. Higher even dimensions remain open.
- `smooth_known_cases` = {1,2,3,5,6,12,56,61} matches Wang–Xu and Wikipedia.
